You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.

It's important to visualize how they relate!**Connecting aligned diamonds**

I’m analyzing how to connect vertically adjacent diamonds that are aligned at the same center. There seems to be a gap to fill between the lower and upper diamonds at specific coordinates. Next, I see potential diagonal connections between two upper diamonds; however, they don’t have aligned endpoints, which complicates things a bit. I also notice some horizontally and vertically aligned diamond pairs in other sections, which might help guide my connections. Counting the centers will give me a clearer picture.
